title: Anthropic says it has confidentially filed IPO papers with the SEC, Axios reports
summary: The filing is listed on Wikipedia's Anthropic entry with an Axios link dated 1 June; no raise size is given.

title: Florida Attorney General Uthmeier sues OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging profit was put ahead of safety
summary: NPR reports it as the first lawsuit by a US state against ChatGPT; the allegations are the state's.

title: Trump signs Executive Order 14409 setting up a voluntary framework for secure deployment of frontier AI models and prioritising action on AI-enabled cybercrime
summary: The order directs agencies to strengthen federal cybersecurity and use AI-enabled defensive tools; engagement with frontier developers before release is voluntary.

title: Google reportedly agrees to pay SpaceX USD 920M a month for compute capacity at xAI data centres
summary: CNBC reports the deal; Wikipedia's SpaceX entry says it covers Nvidia chips from October 2026 to June 2029.

title: OpenAI confirms it has filed for an IPO with the US Securities and Exchange Commission
summary: Wikipedia's OpenAI entry dates the confirmation to 8 June 2026 and gives no raise size.

title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5 with classifier safeguards and limits Mythos 5, with cyber safeguards lifted, to Project Glasswing partners
summary: Classifiers send cyber, biology and chemistry, and distillation requests to Opus 4.8 in under 5% of sessions; both models cost USD 10 and USD 50 per million input and output tokens.

title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calls for stronger AI regulation in an ABC News exclusive
summary: The interview of 10 June is listed on Wikipedia's entry on existential risk from AI.

title: Anthropic suspends access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all users after a US Commerce directive; it says it disagrees with the finding
summary: Wikipedia reports the directive required suspending access for foreign nationals, including Anthropic's own staff, and that US authorities cited national security concerns.

title: Moonshot AI releases and open-sources Kimi K2.7 Code and says it cuts average token use by 30% against K2.6
summary: IT Home reports the release of 12 June with a Hugging Face repository and a 6x-speed variant due 15 June at twice the price; the benchmark gains are the company's own.

title: SpaceX shares begin trading on Nasdaq after an IPO priced at a USD 1.77T valuation, the highest on record
summary: Wikipedia reports the offering priced on 11 June and raised USD 86B against a USD 75B target; SpaceX includes xAI.

title: France says it will replace Palantir with ChapsVision, citing strategic dependence, after the US cut off access to Anthropic's newest models
summary: Wikipedia's Palantir entry attributes the announcement to the DGSI and Prime Minister Lecornu and dates it only to June 2026.

title: Court filings show the Pentagon used a Grok-based version in its Maven Smart System in operations against Iran, per its AI chief Cameron Stanley
summary: Per filings first reported by The Information, the system supported more than 2,000 munitions against 2,000 targets in 96 hours; Wikipedia's Grok entry gives only June 2026.

title: Waymo recalls its robotaxi software after vehicles drove into freeway construction zones
summary: Wired reported the recall in June 2026; Wikipedia's Waymo entry gives no exact day.

title: SpaceX exercises its option to buy Cursor's parent Anysphere in an all-stock deal valued at USD 60B
summary: Reuters and the New York Times report the company will sit under xAI, with closing expected in the third quarter of 2026.

title: Z.ai releases GLM-5.2 with a 1M-token context window; Reuters later reports it closes the frontier gap in coding and agent tasks
summary: Wikipedia's Zhipu AI entry dates the release to 16 June; Reuters on 25 June also reports a planned dual listing.

title: US Commerce Department extends export controls to frontier AI models, requiring licences for certain Anthropic models, Politico reports
summary: Wikipedia's US regulation entry says release to specified trusted partners is authorised; this goes beyond earlier controls on AI hardware.

title: NATO's Palantir-built Maven Smart System reaches full technical operational capability
summary: Wikipedia's Palantir entry dates the milestone to 22 June and adds that a NATO report of 30 June found it compatible with AI systems from Meta and Mistral.

title: Russian government commission approves the bill on supporting AI development, ForkLog reports
summary: The 22 June approval preceded the State Duma's final vote of 8 July; ForkLog's page gives the commission date.

title: Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI have AI model review agreements with the US CAISI; the New York Times reports Washington is pressing Meta to agree
summary: Wikipedia's US regulation entry says the four agreements were in place by the end of June and cites the New York Times article of 23 June.

title: Anthropic accuses Alibaba of illicitly extracting Claude capabilities through about 28.8M interactions from nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts
summary: Reuters reports the activity ran from 22 April to 5 June; the allegation is Anthropic's and the cited summary carries no response from Alibaba.

title: OpenAI and Broadcom announce Jalapeno, a custom inference accelerator, with rollout planned by the end of 2026
summary: OpenAI describes it as its first Intelligence Processor, designed around LLM inference.

title: OpenAI defers the public rollout of GPT-5.6 and starts a limited trusted-partner preview at the US government's request
summary: OpenAI says it previewed the model to the US government first; Reuters reports Washington is seeking early access to frontier models.

title: South Korea's president unveils a USD 576B AI and semiconductor investment drive centred on Samsung and SK Hynix, Reuters reports
summary: The report of 29 June is listed in the Serious Insights June update.

title: US lifts its restrictions on Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, the New York Times reports
summary: Anthropic's own page says both models were redeployed on 1 July; a partial easing for 100+ US organisations had come on 26 June.

title: Putin names AI among three key future technologies at SPIEF plenary and says Russia intends to lead in it
summary: At the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum plenary, Vladimir Putin listed AI with autonomous systems and platform solutions as main future technologies and instructed the government to prepare development strategies for autonomous systems and digital platforms.

title: Chinese AI apps including Qwen and Doubao restrict photo question-answering during the gaokao, Chinese media report
summary: As 12.9 million candidates began China's national college entrance exam, several AI platforms temporarily disabled or limited exam-related features such as photo-based question solving, while platforms cracked down on AI cheating and exam-prediction content.

title: Huawei releases openPangu 2.0, a 505B-parameter model family optimised for Ascend chips, with phased open-sourcing from June 30
summary: At HDC 2026 Huawei's Yu Chengdong announced openPangu 2.0 Pro (505B total, 18B active parameters) and Flash (92B total) with a 512K-token context, and said seven components including training code will be open-sourced in phases starting June 30.

title: ByteDance's Volcano Engine launches Doubao 2.1 Pro and previews Seedance 2.5, reporting 180 trillion daily tokens
summary: At its FORCE conference Volcano Engine released the Doubao 2.1 Pro flagship model for coding and agent tasks, which it says beats Claude Opus 4.6 on several benchmarks at about 80% lower cost, and previewed the Seedance 2.5 video model for July.
